Version 1.1: ESV links with all the tags which are present in the KJV module tagged by Crosswire.org, with much modification
Updates in preparation: 
Version 1.2: Strongs numbers augmented to line up with vocabulary in BDB as defined by OpenScriptures.org and aditional numbers defined by NASB for Greek word in NA/UBS what do not occur in TR
Version 1.3: Tags for missing Hebrew and Greek words added to vocabulary where possible and appended where no lineup is possible. 


HOW TO USE THIS DATA

The numbers refer to the words in the text of the ESV 2011/2016 and Strongs numbers:
* the two-digit numbers are the positions of a word in a verse in ESV 2011, starting at 1. 
* the numbers in <angle brackets> are Strong's Hebrew and Greek vocabulary, where Hebrew has 5 digits starting with zero and Greek has 4 digits. 
* "+" is used to indicate more than one English word is tagged or more than one Hebrew/Greek word is tagged to it. 
  e.g.: $Gen 23:3	02=<00085>	03+04=<06965>	06=<06440>	08=<04191>	10=<01696>+<00559>	13=<01121>+<02845>	

Notes: 
The words of the ESV cannot be supplied for copyright reasons. Any user must apply to Crossway for the rights to use the ESV.
The tagging philosophy is slightly different than that used for the Crosswire KJV module: 
* The KJV module attempted to tag all the English words translated by an individual Hebrew or Greek word. This ESV module attemps to tag the most significant English word.
   eg Gen.1.2 <06440> could be said to represent "face of" but it is tagged only to "face".
* The KJV module frequently had split tags where a Hebrew/Greek word was translated by a phrase interrupted by another tagged word. This ESV module tags only the most significant word. 
   eg Gen.1.1 <07225=רֵאשִׁית=first>+ב could be said to represent "in beginning" but it is tagged only to "beginning"
* The KJV module occasionally tagged the objective article ('eth'). These tags have been removed, though a later version will re-introduce them in a consistent manner.
* Sometimes it is necessary to tag two adjacent English words and sometimes two Hebrew/Greek words tag a single English word, though these have been minimised.
   eg Gen.1.2 <08414=תֹּ֫הוּ=formlessness> is tagged by "without form" because either English word would be misleading
  eg Gen.1.4 "separated" is tagged by <00914=בָּדַל=to separate> & <00996=בַּ֫יִן=between> because there is no English word representing <00996>
